# Caller token format

A caller authenticates with a bearer token minted by `standpipe token create`. The
plaintext is printed exactly once and stored nowhere; the configuration holds only its
SHA-256 hash (`token_hash: "sha256:…"`).

## Format

```text
spd_<token_id>_<secret>_<checksum>
```

| Field | Pattern | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| prefix | `spd` | Fixed. It marks the token type. |
| `token_id` | `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` | The id named in the caller's `token_id`. It may itself contain `_` and `-`, so a token is parsed right to left. |
| secret | `^[A-Za-z0-9]{43}$` | 32 random bytes in base62, left-padded to exactly 43 characters. |
| checksum | `^[0-9a-z]{1,7}$` | CRC-32 (IEEE) of everything before the last `_`, in lower-case base36, unpadded. A truncated copy-paste fails here rather than looking like a wrong secret. |

## Secret-scanning regex

Use this pattern to find leaked tokens in logs, repositories and chat exports:

```text
spd_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}_[A-Za-z0-9]{43}_[0-9a-z]{1,7}
```

It is unanchored on purpose, so it finds a token in the middle of a line. A scanner
should treat only a **full** match of a token-shaped string as a finding.

This is the exact pattern the minter enforces. Before `standpipe token create` prints a
token it runs the token through the gateway's own parser and through this regex, and if
either rejects it the command fails and prints nothing. A token this build mints is
therefore always one this pattern matches in full.

## Authentication

Every authentication failure (malformed header, wrong format, bad checksum, unknown
token id, wrong secret) returns the same `401` with no detail.
